system.summary: A one-step Caesar shift over the 23-letter alphabet was identified from the ciphertext.

conditions.human_role: The contributors supplied their transcription, key and reading.

solution.what: A one-step Caesar shift over the 23-letter alphabet was identified from the ciphertext.
Filed the issue evidence and checked the line replay against the submitted transcription and key.

Page review: the page now states the key and a worked example, the translation and context. The extent chip is measured on cipher letters (1,128 of 1,138 valued) and the 84% is given as a word share (199 of 237 sure words). The two document entries are shown as one text.

outcome.method_basis: A one-step Caesar shift over the 23-letter alphabet was identified from the ciphertext.
outcome.fraction_read_source: aligned.tsv, cipher column: 1,128 of 1,138 cipher letters carry a value; 10 signs are marked '?' (gutter, cancellation, damage). Clear Roman numerals are not counted. Word share is separate: hole-ledger.md gives 185 of 217 words sure on ff. 76r-76v and 14 of 20 on f. 75r (199 of 237, 84%).

credits.note: A second independent decipherment and transcription (model-made, no person checked the transcription), credited to Jacob Houtrouw, agreeing on key and text.

texts.summary: A Latin love-binding conjuration addressed to a rota, enciphered by a one-letter shift: the main text on ff. 76r-76v and a cancelled first version of its opening on f. 75r.

reading_review.by: Codex independent claims review, Claver and Latin
reading_review.note: The Latin and the English were checked against the 39 exact line replays. The formula is coherent in stretches, with unresolved wording at the gutter, in the cancelled opening and at the end. This review used the filed evidence and did not recheck the photographs.

texts.label: Folios 76r and 76v, with the cancelled opening on 75r

gaps.item: a clause on f. 76v that cannot yet be construed, the rota/ruta spelling, unread signs at the gutter and under the cancellation on f. 75r, and the closing numeral

validation.notes: The one-step shift is unique across the alphabet shifts in the prior issue review and the same text was independently replayed; no separate corpus-calibrated test was run.
